subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is malware?
options: A type of firewall used to block network traffic
Malicious software designed to damage or gain unauthorised access to a computer system
A legal document controlling how personal data is used
A backup copy of important files
questions.explain: Malware is any software written to harm a system or gain unauthorised access to it.

questions.q: Which type of malware encrypts a user's files and demands a payment to unlock them?
options: Spyware
Adware
Ransomware
Rootkit
questions.explain: Ransomware encrypts a victim's files and demands payment in exchange for the decryption key.

questions.q: How does a worm differ from a virus?
options: A worm can only infect mobile phones
A worm self-replicates and spreads across networks without attaching to a host file
A worm is a legal form of software testing
A worm cannot cause any damage to data
questions.explain: Unlike a virus, a worm spreads independently and does not need to attach to a host file.

questions.q: A user receives an email appearing to be from their bank asking them to confirm their login details via a link. What kind of attack is this?
options: Phishing
Denial of service
SQL injection
Brute-force attack
questions.explain: Phishing uses fake but legitimate-looking messages to trick users into revealing personal information.

questions.q: What is the main effect of a denial-of-service (DoS) attack?
options: It steals passwords stored in a database
It floods a server with traffic so it cannot respond to legitimate users
It encrypts the user's hard drive
It secretly records the user's keystrokes
questions.explain: A DoS attack overwhelms a server with requests so that genuine users cannot access the service.

questions.q: An attacker uses software that automatically tries thousands of password combinations until it finds the right one. Which attack is this?
options: Pharming
Shouldering
Brute-force attack
Blagging
questions.explain: A brute-force attack systematically tries many combinations to guess a password.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a firewall?
options: To physically lock a server room
To monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on set rules
To permanently delete malware from a system
To encrypt all files on a hard drive
questions.explain: A firewall filters network traffic against set rules to block unauthorised access.

questions.q: What does encryption do to data?
options: Compresses it to save storage space
Scrambles it so it cannot be understood without the decryption key
Deletes it after a set period of time
Copies it to a backup server
questions.explain: Encryption converts data into an unreadable form that requires a key to decrypt.

questions.q: Why do organisations carry out penetration testing?
options: To increase the speed of their network
To deliberately find and fix security weaknesses before attackers exploit them
To back up their databases automatically
To comply with copyright law
questions.explain: Penetration testing simulates attacks to identify vulnerabilities so they can be fixed.

questions.q: How do user access levels help protect data?
options: They encrypt the network cables
They restrict which files and functions each user is allowed to access
They automatically update the operating system
They block all external emails
questions.explain: Access levels limit users to only the data and actions their role requires, reducing misuse.

questions.q: A website asks users for their password and then a code sent to their phone before logging in. Which protection method is this?
options: A CAPTCHA
Two-factor authentication
A firewall
Anti-malware software
questions.explain: Two-factor authentication requires two separate forms of identification to log in.

questions.q: The Computer Misuse Act 1990 primarily makes which of the following illegal?
options: Copying music without permission
Unauthorised access to computer material
Storing personal data insecurely
Selling faulty hardware
questions.explain: The Computer Misuse Act 1990 criminalises unauthorised access to and modification of computer material.

questions.q: Which law governs how organisations must collect, store and use people's personal data in the UK?
options: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Data Protection Act 2018
The Freedom of Information Act 2000
questions.explain: The Data Protection Act 2018 controls how organisations handle people's personal data.

questions.q: What does the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 protect?
options: A person's private data
The intellectual property of original works such as software, music and text
Access to public authority information
Computers from unauthorised access
questions.explain: This Act protects creators' original works from being copied or used without permission.

questions.q: What is a key feature of open source software?
options: The source code is kept secret and cannot be changed
The source code is freely available and can be modified and shared
It can only be used after paying a licence fee
It is always more secure than proprietary software
questions.explain: Open source software makes its source code available for anyone to view, modify and distribute.

questions.q: An employee logs into a colleague's account without permission to read their private files. Which law has most likely been broken?
options: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988
The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Freedom of Information Act 2000
The Health and Safety at Work Act
questions.explain: Gaining unauthorised access to another person's account breaches the Computer Misuse Act 1990.

questions.q: What does the term 'e-waste' refer to?
options: Emails sent in bulk as spam
Discarded electronic devices and equipment
Energy wasted by leaving devices on standby
Data permanently deleted from a hard drive
questions.explain: E-waste is discarded electrical and electronic equipment such as old computers and phones.

questions.q: Why do large data centres have a significant environmental impact?
options: They produce large amounts of paper waste
They consume large amounts of electricity for running and cooling servers
They require frequent replacement of network cables
They emit no carbon but use only water
questions.explain: Data centres use significant electricity to power and cool servers, contributing to carbon emissions.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of recycling old electronic devices?
options: It increases the amount of e-waste sent to landfill
It recovers valuable materials and reduces harmful waste
It uses more raw natural resources
It always deletes personal data automatically
questions.explain: Recycling recovers reusable materials and keeps toxic components out of landfill.

questions.q: A company wants to reduce the environmental impact of its IT equipment. Which action would best help?
options: Replacing all devices with brand-new ones every year
Sending all old equipment to landfill
Upgrading and reusing existing devices for longer before recycling them responsibly
Leaving all computers switched on overnight
questions.explain: Extending device lifespans and recycling responsibly reduces resource use and e-waste.
